# Free, open-source Mac apps by Felix

> Three small, native, open-source macOS apps and two Chrome extensions. None of them needs an account or collects data.

## Apps

- [Clip](https://chengffei.github.io/clip/llms.txt): screenshot, region recording (MP4, GIF) and on-device OCR tool, triggered by double-tapping ⌘. MIT. macOS 14 or later.
- [Leaf](https://chengffei.github.io/leaf/llms.txt): Kindle-style EPUB, MOBI and AZW3 reader with no library; double-click a book to read, close the window to quit. MIT. macOS 15 or later.
- [Uptick](https://chengffei.github.io/uptick/llms.txt): app updater and MacUpdater successor; finds updates from the App Store, Sparkle, Electron feeds and Homebrew, verifies each download, installs it. GPL-3.0. macOS 14 or later.

## Browser extensions

- [Spool](https://chengffei.github.io/spool/llms.txt): Chrome and Edge extension that finds the videos a page loads and saves them as files: direct media, HLS (m3u8) and DASH (mpd) streams merged into one MP4 in the browser, and bilibili in the best quality the user's own account allows. Refuses DRM and YouTube. MIT.
- [Lodestone](https://github.com/chengffei/chrome-extensions/tree/main/lodestone): Chrome and Quark extension that lists magnet links and bare info hashes on a page, guesses resource names from nearby text, copies them and scrolls to them. English and Simplified Chinese. MIT.

## About

Felix is a product manager in energy storage and the first user of every app here. AI didn't make software obsolete; it made it possible for anyone to build it. The apps are open source because software is worth building, for him and for everyone. Paid features may come one day; the free version stays, forever.
